question_text: The Indigenous Cultural Community (ICC) of Barangay Maligaya has been occupying and cultivating a tract of land in the mountains for generations. A mining company claims ownership through a Mineral Production Sharing Agreement (MPSA) with the government. Under RA 8371 (Indigenous Peoples Rights Act), which of the following best describes the legal status of the ICC's claim?

options.text: The ICC has no legal right because the land is classified as mineral land owned by the State.
The ICC may claim ancestral domain title over the area, which includes rights to the land and natural resources.
The ICC can only claim ownership of the surface land, not the minerals beneath it.
The ICC must prove continuous occupation since June 12, 1898 to qualify for ancestral domain.
